newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson, Pharmacia in brand swap.
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson, Pharmacia in brand swap.

text.p: Pharmacia & Upjohn and Johnson & Johnson said Thursday they agreed to swap several over-the-counter drug products in a deal designed to reinforce the market positions of both companies.

Pharmacia's U.S. Consumer Healthcare unit said it acquired Nasalcrom and PediaCare from J&J's McNeil Consumer Products unit and Micatin from J&J Consumer Products. In exchange, J&J said it acquired Motrin IB and Mycitracin from Pharmacia.
"This trade is an outstanding opportunity to expand and strengthen our portfolio," said Michael Valentino, president of Pharmacia Consumer Healthcare U.S.
"It makes sense for both parties, with each benefiting from strong brand heritage," Valentino said.

Brian Perkins, president of J&J's McNeil unit, said, "The acquisition strengthens McNeil's leadership position in the pain reliever category, providing the company with an excellent platform for accelerated growth."
The following products, all sold over-the-counter, were involved in the exchange:
--Nasalcrom, a nasal spray for allergic rhinitis.
--PediaCare, a line of children's cough and cold products.
--Micatin, an anti-fungal application for athlete's foot.
No additional financial terms were associated deal, which was a straight brand swap, said a Pharmacia spokesman.
